note: Bytes the css-parser round trip does not reproduce, one named file per construct. Two kinds, kept apart on purpose. 'open' entries are findings NOT ruled on: none has been accepted, and removing one requires the parser to actually reproduce the byte. 'settled' entries are deliberate compiler behaviour with a citation: the round trip is lossy there BY DESIGN, and the fixture stays in the corpus so that the day the behaviour silently changes, the named-set assertion fails. Adding to either section requires a fixture that isolates the construct and a reason; moving an entry from 'open' to 'settled' requires an owner ruling, not a judgement call by whoever is holding the pen.

selector-attribute-case-flag.css.detail: '[data-x^="y" i]' emits as '[data-x^="y"i]' and '[data-x="y" s]' as '[data-x="y"s]'. This entry originally read that the tight spelling is INVALID CSS. That is wrong and the correction matters: Chromium parses '[data-x="y"i]', CSS.supports() accepts it, and it MATCHES case-insensitively, so the space before the flag is optional and no invalid CSS is being emitted. ('[data-x="y"s]' is rejected there, but so is '[data-x="y" s]' — that engine does not implement the 's' flag at all, which is a support gap, not a whitespace rule.) What remains is real but lower severity: css/scss/jess strip ALL authored whitespace inside an attribute selector, so 'a[ href = "x" i ]' also canonicalises to '[href="x"i]'. Less alone preserves it. The divergence is deliberately pinned on BOTH sides — css-parser/test/discovered-constructs.test.ts:117-126 pins the tight spelling, less-parser/test/discovered-constructs.test.ts:112-124 pins the spaced one as a 'PINNED DEFECT' — precisely so that unifying them fails loudly. Unifying them is an owner call: byte-identity wants the authored bytes preserved (the Less spelling), the existing css canonicalisation wants them stripped.

selector-attribute-unquoted-flag.css.construct: attribute selector case-sensitivity flag on an UNQUOTED ident value
selector-attribute-unquoted-flag.css.detail: SILENT WRONG OUTPUT — the highest-severity entry in this file, and a different defect from selector-attribute-case-flag.css despite the shared mechanism. '[data-x=y i]' emits as '[data-x=yi]', '[lang=en s]' as '[lang=ens]', '[data-x~=y i]' as '[data-x~=yi]' (css, scss and jess; Less is CORRECT and emits '[data-x=y i]'). When the value is QUOTED the space is optional, because a string token and an ident token need no separator — that is why '[data-x="y"i]' is merely cosmetic. Here BOTH sides are ident tokens, so deleting the space does not lose a byte, it MERGES them: the output is the attribute value 'yi' with NO flag, a different selector. Verified in Chromium against a real element: '[data-x=y i]' matches data-x="Y" and not data-x="yi"; '[data-x=yi]' matches data-x="yi" and not data-x="Y" — the match sets are exactly INVERTED, and BOTH selectors parse, so there is no error and no diagnostic anywhere. The cause is that the AttributeSelector reducer joins children with '' (grammar.ts AttributeSelector, and the scss/jess copies), discarding trivia unconditionally rather than where it is safe to discard. Controls confirm the rule is unconditional, not token-aware: '[data-x=y]' round-trips, and '[ data-x = y ]' collapses to '[data-x=y]' — safe only because '=' and ']' are delimiters that cannot fuse with an ident. NOT covered by ledger O7, whose justification is that the stripping is cosmetic and pinned on both sides; no test pins THIS spelling in any dialect. A fix can be surgical and does not disturb O7: emit a separator only where omitting it would fuse two ident tokens, which leaves every quoted case and every delimiter-adjacent case byte-identical to today.

at-rule-namespace-url.css.construct: unquoted url() in a generic at-rule prelude
at-rule-namespace-url.css.detail: '@namespace url(http://example.com/ns);' is REJECTED with 'CSS parser error. Expected: ";", "{".' The quoted form '@namespace ns "http://example.com/ns";' parses. Both spellings are valid per css-namespaces-3 §2, which defines the prelude as a namespace prefix followed by a <string> OR a <url>, so this rejects valid CSS. It is NOT specific to @namespace or to prologue ordering: the failure reproduces with the at-rule ALONE, with no @charset and no @import present, and equally after a rule, so it is the generic statement prelude that cannot take an unquoted url() rather than anything about namespace placement. Found while proving that the spec-correct '@namespace before @import' rejection survived the @charset prologue fix; unrelated to that change and pre-existing.

value-slash-separator.css.construct: authored slash separator in a value
value-slash-separator.css.detail: '12px/1.5', '1/2' and '16/9' emit as '12px / 1.5', '1 / 2', '16 / 9'. Two SETTLED rules collide on exactly this input: 'v5 preserves unoperated values verbatim' says keep '12px/1.5', 'v5 operators and separators are spaced' says emit '12px / 1.5'. The known carve-out that ':nth-*(2n+1)' is NOT spaced shows the spacing rule already admits exceptions. This is a deliberate transform, not a suspected defect, but which of the two rules governs an unoperated authored slash has not been ruled on, and the answer changes emitted CSS for real stylesheets (the 'font' and 'grid-area' shorthands above are ordinary CSS, not computed values). Needs an owner ruling.

empty-blocks.css.construct: a qualified rule or conditional at-rule with an empty block
empty-blocks.css.detail: The whole file emits as the empty string: '.empty {}' and '@media screen {}' are dropped, recursively, so a parent whose only content is a dropping child also drops. This is INTENTIONAL and long-standing, not an accident of a missing branch.
empty-blocks.css.citation: docs/architecture/core/TREE2-DESIGN-SPEC.md:77-80 and :94 name it 'empty-block elision' and :160-161 list it as sourced invariant #4. It is implemented as five deliberate mark-and-rewind sites in packages/core/src/ast/serialize.ts (8839, 8860, 12580, 13912, 14338), each with a doc comment stating the contract, and was introduced by c7d8fe791 and 219585f67 whose messages announce it. It is pinned by packages/jess/test/less/async-eval-lane.test.ts:122-131 (an at-rule is kept alive across an await purely to decide emptiness), packages/core/src/ast/__tests__/import-at-rule.test.ts:602, packages/syntax/scss/scss-parser/test/public-parse.test.ts:269-273, and by zero-byte expected-output fixtures in the Less corpus (tests-unit/at-rules-empty-block). The one deliberate exception is a body containing a BLOCK comment, which keeps the block renderable; a line comment does not.
empty-blocks.css.consequence: Byte-identity and empty-block elision cannot both hold for this input. Elision wins; the fixture stays so that if elision ever silently stops, this file becomes identical and the named-set assertion fails.
